scroll-41.name: Split-word intro with expanding clip-path image
scroll-41.text:
- **What you see:** A white screen with an eight-letter word in huge black capitals across the middle and, behind it, a small portrait window rotated 30 degrees showing part of a photo. Scrolling pushes the two halves of the word apart (each scaling 10x and sliding off its side) while the window turns upright and opens to the full viewport and the photo zooms out from 2x to 1x. The photo then scrolls away and a black content block follows. (Described from code; no preview video.)
- **Use for:** hero that opens an editorial or portfolio page. Needs one wide hero photo (demo 2400x1600), a short word split into two letter groups, then normal page content.
- **How it works:**
  - `.header` (fixed, centred, z-index 2) holds two `.letters` flex groups of single-letter divs at 18vw. `.website-content` is `position: fixed; top: 0` and contains `.img-holder` (100vh, `clip-path: polygon(37.5% 20%, 62.5% 20%, 62.5% 80%, 37.5% 80%)`, `rotate(30deg)`, its img at `scale(2)`) and `.content-holder`.
  - Because everything is fixed, JS sets `body.style.height` to the content height + 2 * innerHeight on DOMContentLoaded to create scroll length.
  - Four separate `gsap.to` tweens, each with its own ScrollTrigger and no trigger element (the document): start "top top", end "+=200%", scrub 1, ease power2.inOut, no pin. Targets: first `.letters` x -3 * innerWidth and scale 10; last `.letters` x +3 * innerWidth and scale 10; `.img-holder` rotation 0 and clipPath to the full rectangle; `.img-holder img` scale 1.
  - A fifth ScrollTrigger (trigger `.website-content`, start "-0.1% top", end "bottom bottom") is a hand-made pin release: onEnter sets `.website-content` to `position: absolute; top: 195%`, onLeaveBack back to `fixed; top: 0`.
- **Adapt:** rebuild rather than copy: put the word and ima

menu-8.name: Product-row overlay with floating thumbnail
menu-8.text: - **What you see:** Clicking the two-bar burger wipes a white full-screen layer down from the top. Brand, close X and footer fade up, thin rules draw left to right, and four product titles (index + name), each breaking its rule at a different point, rise in. Hovering a row dims the others to 20% while a 420x280 photo fades in and glides to that row's own position; a footer counter updates. - **Use for:** nav menu, full-screen overlay type; doubles as a product or project index. Needs 4 titles and one image per row. - **How it works:** - `.menu` (fixed, inset 0, z-index 20) starts at `clip-path: inset(0 0 100% 0)` with `pointer-events: none`. - One paused timeline: clipPath to `inset(0 0 0% 0)` (1s, power4.inOut) at 0; `.row__line` `scaleX` 0 to 1 (origin left, .7s, stagger .05, power3.out) at .45; `.menu__top` and `.menu__foot` fade in with `y` 20 to 0 at .5; `.row__title` opacity and `y` 30 to 0 (.6s, stagger .06) at .55. - Wiring: `#js-toggle` and `#js-close` are real buttons. Open state is derived (`!tl.reversed() && tl.progress() > 0`); opening adds `.is-open`, sets `aria-hidden="false"` and plays; closing reverses. Esc closes. - Each `li.row` is line + `a.row__title` + line (`.row__line`); their inline `flex` values place the title. - Hover: `mouseenter` calls `positionThumb(row)`: x = width × `data-thumb-x`/1000, y = centre + `data-offset`/2.5, applied with `quickTo` (.5s, power3). Images are pre-mounted in `#js-thumb`; the one matching `data-img` fades in, the rest out. Dimming is CSS: `.rows:has(.row:hover) .row:not(:hover) { opacity: .2 }`. - **Adapt:** per row set `data-img`, `data-thumb-x` (0-1000), `data-offset` and the two inline `flex` values (the `data-*-flex` attributes are not read), and add a matching `` to `#js-thumb`; the counter's "/

scroll-61.name: Text fill wipe and merging triple heading
scroll-61.text: - **What you see:** On a near-black page, a large grey paragraph turns white from the top down as it passes mid-screen. Three stacked copies of a huge "WHAT I DO" wordmark slide in from alternating sides; the section pins, the outer copies slide behind the middle one, and the single wordmark shrinks to a small label that ends up just above the next paragraph. - **Use for:** pinned storytelling section / text reveal for an about or services block. Needs two paragraphs and one heading exported as an SVG wordmark (white paths); the hero and outro portraits are filler. - **How it works:** - Text fill: JS copies each `.animate-text` h1's text into `data-text`; CSS draws `::before {content: attr(data-text); color: #fff; clip-path: inset(0 0 var(--clip-value) 0)}` over the grey text. `ScrollTrigger.create({trigger: el, start: "top 50%", end: "bottom 50%", scrub: 1, onUpdate})` moves `--clip-value` from 100% to 0%. - `.services` (100svh flex column) holds three `.services-header` rows, each an `` of the SVG on an opaque `#1a1a1a` strip. CSS starts rows 1 and 3 at `translateX(100%)`, row 2 at `translateX(-100%)` with `z-index: 2`. - Slide-in: `{trigger: ".services", start: "top bottom", end: "top top", scrub: 1, onUpdate}` brings x to 0 on all three with `gsap.set`. - Pin: `{trigger: ".services", start: "top top", end: "+=" + innerHeight * 2, pin: true, pinSpacing: false, scrub: 1, onUpdate}`. First half: row 1 `y` to 100%, row 3 `y` to -100%. Second half: all rows `scale` 1 to 0.1 (0.3 when `innerWidth <= 1000`). - With `pinSpacing: false`, `.services-copy` carries `margin-top: 155svh` to provide the scroll room. - **Adapt:** export your own heading as SVG; the three rows are addressed by index. Keep the 155svh margin in step with the two-viewport pin. `end` is m

scroll-47.name: Pinned photo pile then scatter
scroll-47.text:
- **What you see:** A centred serif headline pins. Four rounded photos rise from below one after another and pile on top of it, each slightly rotated. Further scrolling pulls the pile apart: the photos straighten and settle at the four corners around the headline, which becomes readable again.
- **Use for:** pinned storytelling section. Needs one headline and exactly four landscape images (7:5), plus intro and outro headlines.
- **How it works:**
  - `.spotlight` (100svh) holds `.spotlight-header h1` and an absolute `.spotlight-images` layer; each `.spotlight-img` sits at `top: 50%; left: 50%`, width `clamp(20rem, 25vw, 40rem)`, starting at `translate(-50%, 200%)`.
  - `ScrollTrigger.create({trigger: ".spotlight", start: "top top", end: "+" + innerHeight * 6 + "px", pin: true, pinSpacing: true, scrub: 1, onUpdate})`. The end is written without `=` and is meant as six viewports of pin; use `"+=" + innerHeight * 6` when porting.
  - Phase 1 (progress 0-0.45): image i starts at `[0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3][i]`; y goes 200% to -50% with a hand-written cubic ease-out; rotation stays `[5, -3, 3.5, -1][i]` degrees.
  - Phase 2 (0.5-0.95): starts at `[0.5, 0.55, 0.6, 0.65][i]`; x/y move from -50%/-50% to `spotlightImgFinalPos` (`[-140, -140], [40, -130], [-160, 40], [20, 30]`, % of the image's own size) while rotation eases to 0.
  - Frames are applied with `gsap.set(img, {transform: "translate(x%, y%) rotate(r deg)"})`. Lenis: `lenis.on("scroll", ScrollTrigger.update)`, raf on `gsap.ticker`, `lagSmoothing(0)`.
- **Adapt:** offsets, rotations and end positions are JS arrays for four images (no data-attributes); extend all of them to change the count. End positions scale with image size, so check narrow screens (h1 goes full width under 1000px). `end` uses innerHeight at load; no resize

scroll-19.name: Corner-connected grid item reveals
scroll-19.text:
- **What you see:** A dark page with images of different widths, one per row on an 8-column grid, each sitting left or right of the previous one like a staircase. As an item scrolls in, its image scales up from the top corner nearest the previous image while the picture inside zooms out from 5x, and the caption slides in from that side. Three alternative pages change the motion (see Variants).
- **Use for:** gallery grid. Needs 13-15 images (1.5:1 landscape, or square for demo 4), each with a short title and year.
- **How it works:**
  - Markup: `.grid > figure.grid__item[style="--r; --c; --s"] > .grid__item-img` (overflow hidden, `aspect-ratio: var(--img-ratio)`) `> .grid__item-img-inner` (CSS background), plus an absolutely positioned `figcaption.grid__item-caption`. From 53em up: `grid-template-columns: repeat(8, 1fr)`, `grid-column: var(--c) / span var(--s)`, `grid-row: var(--r)`; below that a single column.
  - Side detection per item: `isLeftSide = prev && item.offsetLeft + item.offsetWidth <= prev.offsetLeft + 1`; `originX = isLeftSide ? 100 : 0`, so transforms pivot on the top corner that faces the previous item.
  - Demo 1, one timeline per item: `scrollTrigger: { trigger: item, start: "top bottom-=15%", end: "+=100%", scrub: true }`, no pin, ease power4: `.grid__item-img` scale 0 to 1 (`transformOrigin: originX% 0%`), `.grid__item-img-inner` scale 5 to 1, caption `xPercent` 100 or -100 to 0 with opacity 0 to 1 (power1).
  - Smooth scroll: `new Lenis({ lerp: 0.15, smoothWheel: true })`, `lenis.on('scroll', () => ScrollTrigger.update())`, own `requestAnimationFrame` loop calling `lenis.raf(time)` (not gsap.ticker). Starts after `imagesLoaded` on the background divs.
- **Variants:** body class `demo-N` sets colours, `--img-ratio` and the default `--s`.
  - `index

scroll-15.name: Horizontal sentence with tumbling letters
scroll-15.text:
- **What you see:** A full-height section pins and one very large single-line sentence travels from the right edge to the left as you scroll. Letters enter scattered above or below the line and rotated, and each eases onto the baseline by the time it is about a third of the way from the left edge.
- **Use for:** horizontal scroll text reveal. Needs one sentence; no images.
- **How it works:**
  - Markup: `section.Horizontal` (100vh, overflow hidden, flex, vertically centred) `> .container > h3.Horizontal__text.heading-xl`. The h3 is `display: flex; width: max-content; white-space: nowrap; gap: 4vw; padding-left: 100vw`, font-size `clamp(2rem, 10vw, 12rem)`.
  - `SplitText.create(".Horizontal__text", { type: "chars, words" })`; the word wrappers become the flex items.
  - Container tween: `scrollTween = gsap.to(text, { xPercent: -100, ease: "none", scrollTrigger: { trigger: ".Horizontal", pin: true, end: "+=5000px", scrub: true } })` (start defaults to "top top").
  - Per character: `gsap.from(char, { yPercent: "random(-200, 200)", rotation: "random(-20, 20)", ease: "back.out(1.2)", scrollTrigger: { trigger: char, containerAnimation: scrollTween, start: "left 100%", end: "left 30%", scrub: 1 } })`.
- **Adapt:** change the sentence in the HTML. The 5000px distance, the random ranges and the 100%/30% window are hard-coded (derive `end` from `text.scrollWidth` for other lengths); nothing is data-attribute driven. In a Vite site import `gsap`, `ScrollTrigger`, `SplitText` from npm and ignore the script list: the gsap core URL in `dist/index.html` reads `unpkg.co` (not `.com`) and the codepen.io plugin builds are not for production. Page base styles come from a remote CodePen stylesheet (`codepen.io/GreenSock/pen/xxmzBrw.css`) that is not included. One ScrollTrigger per chara

scroll-34.name: Pinned zoom through a window frame
scroll-34.text:
- **What you see:** A dark cabin wall with an airplane window fills the screen, blue sky showing through the pane and serif headings in the corners. Scrolling zooms the window until its frame leaves the screen, the headings flying outward with it, while the sky photo drifts upward into clouds. Near the end a large paragraph rises from the bottom over the clouds; a plain outro follows.
- **Use for:** hero as a pinned storytelling opener. Needs one frame PNG with a transparent opening (demo 2400x1350), one very tall background photo (demo 3481x5221), two corner headings with small copy, one long statement.
- **How it works:**
  - `.hero` (100svh, `perspective: 1000px`, overflow hidden) stacks four absolute layers in DOM order: `.sky-container` (350svh tall), `.hero-copy` (centred h1), `.window-container` (the PNG, object-fit cover), `.hero-header` (two columns, `preserve-3d`).
  - One ScrollTrigger: trigger `.hero`, start "top top", end `+=innerHeight*3`, pin true, pinSpacing true, scrub 1. There is no tween: onUpdate calls `gsap.set` from `self.progress`, so `scrub: 1` adds no smoothing.
  - Progress 0-0.5: `.window-container` scale 1 to 4 (held after); `.hero-header` gets the same scale plus `z = progress * 500`.
  - Whole range: `.sky-container` y = -progress * (its height - viewport height). 0.66-1: `.hero-copy` yPercent 100 to 0.
  - Lenis wiring: `new Lenis()`, `lenis.on("scroll", ScrollTrigger.update)`, `gsap.ticker.add(t => lenis.raf(t * 1000))`, `gsap.ticker.lagSmoothing(0)`.
- **Adapt:** swap the PNG (any image with a transparent opening that clears the viewport at 4x) and the tall photo, and compress both (6.3 MB together). Every number is hard-coded in JS; no data-attributes, and CSS vars only hold colours. `end` and the sky travel are computed once at load: m

scroll-53.name: Nine-tile mask image reveal
scroll-53.text: - **What you see:** On a white fashion-brand page, whenever a row of images reaches the lower quarter of the screen each image builds itself from a 3×3 grid of tiles: every tile grows out of its own top-left corner, in diagonal order from top-left to bottom-right, in about one second. It plays once and is not tied to scroll position. - **Use for:** image reveal for gallery grids, lookbooks, product or team grids. Any number of images; text is ordinary page copy. - **How it works:** - `createMasks()` appends nine `.mask.m-1` to `.m-9` divs to every `.img` (`position: relative; aspect-ratio: 4/5`). Each mask is absolute, full size, and carries the whole picture as a CSS background (`.img-1 .mask { background: url(./assets/img3.jpg) ...; background-size: cover }`, defined for `img-1` to `img-17`). - `initialClipPaths[9]` are zero-area polygons at each cell's top-left corner (e.g. `polygon(33% 0%, 33% 0%, 33% 0%, 33% 0%)`); `finalClipPaths[9]` are the cell rectangles, overlapping 0.5% to hide seams. - Per image: `gsap.timeline({scrollTrigger: {trigger: row, start: "top 75%"}})`. No scrub, no pin, default play-once. - The timeline tweens `clipPath` on diagonal groups `[m-1]`, `[m-2, m-4]`, `[m-3, m-5, m-7]`, `[m-6, m-8]`, `[m-9]` at `index * 0.125`s, each `duration: 0.5, ease: "power2.out", stagger: 0.1`. - Lenis: `lenis.on("scroll", ScrollTrigger.update)`, raf on `gsap.ticker`, `lagSmoothing(0)`. - **Adapt:** to add an image, put a `.img.img-N` div in a `.row` and add a matching background rule in CSS (not `` tags, so no alt text or lazy loading). A `.img` without a numbered class is a deliberate blank cell. For another grid size rewrite both clip-path arrays. Nine layers per image: keep sources compressed. The demo layout has no breakpoints. No reduced-motio

scroll-9.name: Pinned SVG-mask blinds image transitions
scroll-9.text:
- **What you see:** A full-screen stage stays pinned while you scroll. The first image appears through 30 horizontal slats opening one after another from the bottom up; a large serif caption wipes in, holds and wipes out; then the next image opens over it the same way. Three thin segments at the bottom fill with progress. The motion trails the scroll by a couple of seconds.
- **Use for:** pinned storytelling section: 3 (or more) full-bleed images, each with a heading, a sub-heading and a short paragraph.
- **How it works:**
  - `.stage` (500vh) > `.layers` (`position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100vh`) holding three stacked `<svg class="layer" preserveAspectRatio="none">`. Each has an `<image preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice" mask="url(#maskN)">` and a `<mask maskUnits="userSpaceOnUse">` with a black `<rect>` plus an empty `<g id="blindsN">`. `.txt` captions and `.progress-bar` sit on top.
  - `updateLayout()` sets every viewBox to `0 0 100 (innerHeight / innerWidth * 100)`; `createBlinds()` fills the `<g>` with `BLIND_COUNT = 30` strips, each two white rects of height 0 on the strip's centre line. `openBlinds()` tweens `attr: {y, height}` so strips open from their centre (`power3.out`, stagger 0.02, bottom strip first).
  - Master timeline: `scrollTrigger: {trigger: '.stage', start: 'top top', end: 'bottom bottom', scrub: 2.5, anticipatePin: 1, invalidateOnRefresh: true}`; no `pin` (CSS sticky does it). Per layer: `openBlinds`, then `textIn` at `'-=0.3'` (`clipPath` to `inset(0% 0% 0% 0%)`, y 40 to 0, 1.5s `expo.out`), then `textOut` at `'+=0.8'` (`inset(0% 0% 100% 0%)`, y -30, 1.2s `power2.inOut`).
  - Progress: a second `ScrollTrigger.create` on `.stage` (scrub 0.3) writes each `.fill` width in `onUpdate`.
  - Lenis `{lerp: 0.15, smoothWheel: true, smoothTouch: !isTo

scroll-40.name: Image splits into three flipping cards
scroll-40.text:
- **What you see:** A panoramic image sits in the middle of a dark pinned section. As you scroll it narrows slightly and a title fades in above it; then it breaks into three portrait cards with gaps and rounded corners. Further on the cards flip over one after another to coloured backs carrying a number and a label, the outer two tilting outward.
- **Use for:** pinned storytelling section for three services, pillars or steps. Needs one image pre-sliced into three 5:7 pieces (demo: three 800x1120 JPEGs), a heading, and a number plus short label per card.
- **How it works:**
  - `.sticky` (100svh, flex centre) > `.sticky-header h1` + `.card-container` (width 75%, `perspective: 1000px`) > 3 `.card` (`flex: 1; aspect-ratio: 5/7; preserve-3d; transform-origin: top`), each with `.card-front` (img) and `.card-back` (rotateY 180deg), both `backface-visibility: hidden`.
  - Inside `gsap.matchMedia()` for "(min-width: 1000px)": one ScrollTrigger, trigger `.sticky`, start "top top", end `+=innerHeight*4`, pin true, pinSpacing true, scrub 1, all logic in onUpdate.
  - Set directly from progress: container width 75% to 60% over 0-0.25; title y 40 to 0 and opacity 0 to 1 over 0.1-0.25.
  - Threshold-fired tweens (time-based, reversed when scrolling back, guarded by two flags): at 0.35 `gap` 0 to 20px and every card's border-radius to 20px (0.5s power3.out); at 0.7 `.card` rotationY 180 (0.75s power3.inOut, stagger 0.1) while `#card-1` and `#card-3` get y 30 and rotationZ -15 / +15.
- **Adapt:** the ids `#card-1` to `#card-3` and the card count are hard-coded; back colours are CSS vars `--card-1` to `--card-3`. Below 1000px there is no animation: cards stack and only the text backs show. The debounced resize handler re-runs `initAnimations()`, which kills every ScrollTrigger on the pa

slider-17.name: Fullscreen wipe slider with gooey blur titles
slider-17.text:
- **What you see:** A full-viewport image with a large uppercase title in the centre and dashed-border arrow buttons at the left and right edges. Clicking an arrow wipes the next image in from that side while both images drift sideways in parallax; the old title dissolves into a soft liquid blob and the new one condenses out of blur.
- **Use for:** slider / hero. 5 full-bleed images (demo 2400×1350, ~0.6 MB each) with a 2-3 word title each.
- **How it works:**
  - Data: `carouselSlides` array (`title`, `image`). Input: `.prev-btn` / `.next-btn` clicks only; the index wraps with modulo (infinite); `isAnimating` blocks clicks for 1.5s. No drag, wheel, keys or autoplay.
  - `animateSlide(direction)` appends a new `.img > img` to `.carousel-images`, animates the container's `clipPath` from a zero-width polygon on the entering side to the full rect and its img from `x: ±slideOffset` to 0, while the outgoing img moves the other way; all 1.5s with CustomEase `hop` (`M0,0 C0.071,0.505 0.192,0.726 0.318,0.852 0.45,0.984 0.504,1 1,1`). Old nodes are removed on complete. `slideOffset` is 500, or 100 under 1000px.
  - Caption sync: all titles are pre-built as stacked `.slide-title-container > h1.title`, split into `.word` by SplitText after `document.fonts.ready`. `updateActiveTextSlide()` tweens the other slides' words to `blur(75px)` / opacity 0 (2.5s, power1.out) and the current ones to `blur(0px)` / opacity 1 (2s, power3.out).
  - The goo: `h1.title` has `filter: url(#blur-matrix) blur(0.25px)`; the inline SVG `feColorMatrix` (alpha × 255 - 140) thresholds the blurred words.
- **Adapt:** edit the array; add autoplay, swipe and arrow keys if wanted. Image and font paths use `./public/...`: fine in dev or static hosting, wrong after `vite build` (use `/carousel/...`), and the cla

text-16.name: Cursor-repelled letters and words
text-16.text:
- **What you see:** A dark screen with two huge headlines and a justified paragraph between them. Moving the cursor near the text pushes nearby letters (headlines) or whole words (paragraph) straight away from the pointer, by up to 300px for the closest ones; they drift back with a soft lag once the cursor has moved on.
- **Use for:** cursor/hover effect on text: a hero headline or a short statement paragraph. Needs only text.
- **How it works:**
  - `animateTextElements(selector, splitBy)` empties each container and rebuilds it from its `textContent` as `<span class="word">` or `<span class="letter">` (inline-block, `will-change: transform`). It is called for `.anime-text` with "words" and `.anime-header` with "letters".
  - 100ms later each span's centre (`getBoundingClientRect`, viewport coordinates) is stored once as `originalX/Y`.
  - Each container adds its own `mousemove` listener on `document`: for spans whose stored centre is within `radius = 150` px of the cursor, `force = (1 - distance / radius) * 300` and the target offset is the unit vector pointing away from the cursor times that force; otherwise the target is 0.
  - Each container also runs its own rAF loop: `current += (target - current) * 0.1`, then `transform: translate(x, y)` is written on every span, every frame.
- **Adapt:** tune `radius`, `maxDisplacement` and `lerpFactor` (constants inside the listener and loop). Centres are measured once: after a resize, scroll or late font swap the hit areas are off, so re-measure, and use page coordinates if the text scrolls (the demo is a fixed 100vh box with `overflow: hidden`). Splitting discards inner markup. Mouse-only, no touch. The loops never stop, and every span has `will-change: transform` plus a style write per frame, so cost grows with text length (

webgl-17.name: Scroll noise-dissolve hero to solid colour
webgl-17.text:
- **What you see:** A dark illustrated forest hero with a huge thin yellow title. As you scroll, a cream colour climbs from the bottom with a torn, grainy edge until it covers the image; two tree-branch cut-outs at the sides shoot upward at different speeds; a centred uppercase sentence appears word by word on the cream.
- **Use for:** hero / section transition. One tall background image, two transparent foreground cut-outs, a title and one sentence.
- **How it works:**
  - Layout: `.hero__row` is 185vh tall and holds `.hero__bg` (absolute, cover), `canvas.hero-canvas` (absolute, hero-sized, not fixed or pinned), `.hero__top` (100vh title) and `.hero__content` (bottom 125vh, the `h2`).
  - WebGL: OrthographicCamera(-1,1,1,-1) + `PlaneGeometry(2,2)` with a transparent `ShaderMaterial`. Fragment: `d = uv.y - uProgress * 1.2 + fbm(centeredUv * 15) * uSpread`; `alpha = 1 - smoothstep(-px, px, d)`; colour = `uColor`. Uniforms: `uProgress`, `uResolution`, `uColor` (`CONFIG.color` #ebf5df), `uSpread` 0.5. No textures.
  - Driver: the Lenis `scroll` event sets `uProgress = min(scroll / (hero.offsetHeight - innerHeight) * CONFIG.speed, 1.1)`: absolute page scroll, not a ScrollTrigger.
  - Text: SplitText words on `.hero__content h2`; a ScrollTrigger (`trigger: '.hero__content'`, `start: 'top 25%'`, `end: 'bottom 100%'`, `onUpdate`) fades each word from 0.1 to 1 in sequence.
  - Parallax: `.hero__twig--left` to y -2000 and `.hero__twig--right` to y -3500, `ease: 'none'`, `scrub: true`, trigger `.hero`, `top top` to `bottom top`.
- **Adapt:** does not run as shipped: the HTML loads `script.js` as a classic script although it uses bare ES imports, and `import './index.scss'` points to a missing file. Put it in Vite (`npm i three gsap lenis`, `type="module"`, delete the scss import)

hero-7.name: Capsule preloader into hero reveal
hero-7.text: - **What you see:** The page opens on a pill-shaped progress capsule; the logo slides in letter by letter with a two-line tagline while the bar fills in three uneven steps. Text slides out, then the pill-shaped hole grows to 6x so the hero photo is revealed through it while the photo settles from 1.5x to 1x. Title letters and sub-copy rise out of masked lines; a looping smoke video sits over the photo. - **Use for:** hero + preloader. Needs one strong full-bleed photo (plus a mobile crop), a one-word brand title, a 3-line subtitle and one sentence. - **How it works:** - `.preloader-mask` is a fixed full-screen panel with `mask: linear-gradient(...), url(preloader-bg.svg) center/42% no-repeat; mask-composite: exclude` (plus `-webkit-mask-composite: xor`), which cuts a pill-shaped hole. The timeline scales it to 6 (4s, power3.out), then fades it out. - `.preloader-progress` (pill, overflow hidden, scale .86 to 1) holds `.preloader-progress-bar`, animated scaleX 0 to 1 in 3 random steps over 3.5s by `animateProgress()`. - Hand-rolled splitters: `splitCharsInline` wraps chars in `.inline-mask > .inline-char`; lines use `.line-mask > .reveal-line`; all animate xPercent/yPercent 100 to 0 (power4, stagger .05-.1). - `.hero-img` scales 1.5 to 1 as the mask opens; `.smoke-video` overlays at opacity .5 with mix-blend-mode hard-light. - **Adapt:** swap the photo, copy and the SVG (any white shape becomes the window). Drop or re-encode the 30 MB video. Under 768px the background is replaced by an inline ``. The loader is a fixed ~7s timeline, not tied to real loading, and there is no reduced-motion path: add both.

scroll-39.name: Scattered tags merge into a search bar
scroll-39.text:
- **What you see:** A dark section with a serif headline and seven small labelled pills scattered around it. Once pinned, the headline slides up and out, the labels fade, and the pills drift to the centre while shrinking into round dots that stack into one. That dot drops lower and stretches into a wide rounded search bar; its placeholder text and a new headline with sub-copy fade in above it.
- **Use for:** pinned storytelling section that turns a feature list into a product pitch. Needs 7 short tags, two headlines, one sentence, a placeholder string, and optionally a faint background graphic.
- **How it works:**
  - `.spotlight` (100svh) holds `.spotlight-content` (background image + h1), `.header > .header-content`, `.features` (7 absolutely positioned `.feature`, each with `.feature-bg` and `.feature-content p`) and `.search-bar` (3rem circle, opacity 0).
  - JS places each pill from a hard-coded `featureStartPositions` array (top/left in %) and measures every `.feature-bg` at load.
  - One ScrollTrigger: trigger `.spotlight`, start "top top", end `+=innerHeight*3`, pin true, pinSpacing true, scrub 1; onUpdate calls `gsap.set` from `self.progress` (no tween, so no scrub smoothing).
  - 0-0.333: `.spotlight-content` y 0 to -100%. 0-0.1: labels fade out. 0-0.5: each pill's top/left lerp to 50%/50% while its background lerps to 3rem x 3rem, radius 0.5 to 25rem, border 0.125 to 0.35rem.
  - At 0.5 `.features` is hidden and `.search-bar` shown (an identical 3rem circle). 0.5-0.75: bar width 3 to 25rem (20rem under 1000px), height 3 to 5rem, translateY -50% to 200%. 0.75-1: bar text and `.header-content` (y -50 to 0) fade in.
- **Adapt:** the positions array needs one entry per `.feature` (a missing entry throws). Sizes, thresholds and positions are hard-coded in JS; CSS

scroll-35.name: Pinned icons shrink into inline text slots
scroll-35.text:
- **What you see:** A dark hero with a title and a row of five large rounded icons along the bottom edge. On scroll the title fades, the icons rise one after another, then the row shrinks into the middle of the screen while the background snaps to light. The five small icons then travel, down first and then sideways, into empty slots inside a large centred sentence whose fragments fade in around them in random order.
- **Use for:** hero as a pinned storytelling section. Needs exactly 5 square icons (demo: 2000x2000 PNG, ~60 KB each), a title with tagline, and one sentence cut into 6 fragments with 5 icon slots.
- **How it works:**
  - DOM: `.hero` > `.hero-header`, `.animated-icons` (`position: fixed` row at the bottom with 5 `.animated-icon`), `h1.animated-text` with hidden inline `.placeholder-icon` slots (3.75rem; 1.875rem under 1000px) between `.text-segment` spans (opacity 0).
  - One ScrollTrigger: trigger `.hero`, start "top top", end `+=innerHeight*8`, pin true, pinSpacing true, scrub 1; onUpdate sets everything from `self.progress` (no tween, so no scrub smoothing).
  - 0-0.3: row y to -30vh; each icon carries a counter-offset released with a 0.1 stagger; header fades out by 0.15.
  - 0.3-0.6: row moves to viewport centre and scales to `60px / iconWidth` (30px under 1000px); at the midpoint `.hero` background switches #141414 to #e3e3db (CSS transition 0.3s).
  - 0.6-0.75: row hidden; 5 clones (`.duplicate-icon`, absolute on `<body>`, stored in `window.duplicateIcons`) move from each icon's rect to its placeholder's rect, vertical half first, then horizontal.
  - 0.75-1: clones sit on the placeholders; segments fade in, order shuffled once at load, 0.03 apart.
- **Adapt:** icon count must equal placeholder count; colours, sizes and thresholds are hard-coded in

scroll-63.name: Pinned hero slit-and-spin transition
scroll-63.text:
- **What you see:** The pinned full-screen hero photo is squeezed into a thin dark vertical bar, uncovering a pale layer with a short text block at each side. The bar rotates 65°, turns red and shrinks to nothing while the text blocks move to the centre. Two half-screen images then wipe in (left from the top, right from the bottom) and a centred headline rises line by line.
- **Use for:** hero / pinned storytelling section. Needs one hero photo and headline, two short titled text blocks, two tall outro images and a closing headline.
- **How it works:**
  - `.hero` (100svh) stacks three absolute layers: `.hero-bg-content` (z 0, pale, two `.hero-bg-content-copy`), `.hero-outro-content` (z 1, two `.hero-outro-img` clipped to zero height, centred h3) and `.hero-fg-content` (z 2: image, h1, `.hero-fg-overlay-dark`, `.hero-fg-overlay`).
  - `ScrollTrigger.create({trigger: ".hero", start: "top top", end: "+=" + innerHeight * 5 + "px", pin: true, pinSpacing: true, scrub: 1, onUpdate})`. Each phase is `gsap.utils.clamp` + `interpolate` on `self.progress`, applied with `gsap.set`.
  - Progress 0-0.25: foreground `clipPath` polygon narrows from 0%-100% to 48%-52% wide; dark overlay opacity 0 to 1. 0.25-0.45: `rotate` 0 to 65.
  - 0.45-0.65: `scale` 1 to 0, copy blocks `x` to +100% / -100%, red overlay fades in over 0.45-0.50. 0.65-0.85: the left image's clip opens downward, the right one's upward.
  - At 0.9 a time-based tween raises the h3 lines (`SplitText.create(h3, {type: "lines", mask: "lines", linesClass: "line"})`): `y: "0%"`, 0.75s, stagger 0.1, `power3.out`; reversed when progress drops below 0.9.
  - Lenis: `lenis.on("scroll", ScrollTrigger.update)`, raf on `gsap.ticker`, `lagSmoothing(0)`.
- **Adapt:** colours are CSS variables `--base-100/200/300`; phase boundaries and

scroll-31.name: Dual-column sine-wave text index
scroll-31.text:
- **What you see:** On a black page two columns of uppercase mono labels (project names left, brand names right) run down the screen, each row pushed sideways so the columns form mirrored sine waves that travel as you scroll. The row nearest the viewport centre turns white in both columns, and a small thumbnail between the columns stays centred and switches to that row's image.
- **Use for:** text reveal as a scroll-driven index (clients, projects, credits). Needs 20-50 paired short labels and one small image per row (demo: 48 rows, 24 webp of 5-70 KB).
- **How it works:**
  - Markup: `.dual-wave-wrapper[data-wave-number][data-wave-speed]` > `.wave-column-left` + `.image-thumbnail-wrapper > img.image-thumbnail` + `.wave-column-right`; rows are `.animated-text`, the left ones carry `data-image`.
  - `ScrollTrigger.create({ trigger: wrapper, start: "top bottom", end: "bottom top", onUpdate })`: no scrub, no pin. Smooth scrolling is `ScrollSmoother.create({ smooth: 1.5, normalizeScroll: true })` on `#smooth-wrapper > #smooth-content`.
  - Per row: `phase = waveNumber * index + waveSpeed * progress * 2PI - PI/2`; `x = (sin(phase) + 1) / 2 * (columnWidth - widestText)`, negated for the right column and applied through `gsap.quickTo(el, "x", { duration: 0.6, ease: "power4.out" })`, which gives the trailing feel.
  - `findClosestToViewportCenter()` picks the row nearest mid-screen: it gets `.focused` in both columns (CSS colour #4d4d4d to white, 300ms) and its `data-image` becomes the thumbnail `src`; the thumbnail's `y` is re-set each update to stay at viewport centre, clamped to the wrapper.
  - `preloadImages()` loads every `data-image` before `body.loading` is removed and `init()` runs.
- **Adapt:** edit the rows in HTML (same count in both columns; demo labels are real br

scroll-51.name: Slanted clip-path project sections
scroll-51.text:
- **What you see:** Each project is a 150svh full-bleed image. Its top edge enters as a slanted cut that flattens until the image fills the screen, while the white title rises letter by letter from behind masks. On leaving, the bottom edge folds up into a slanted wedge, exposing the next project's opening cut.
- **Use for:** section transition / image reveal for a work or case-study list. Needs one large image and a short title per project (five supplied), plus intro and outro headings.
- **How it works:**
  - `.work-item` (150svh, `overflow: hidden`) contains `.work-item-img` (absolute, full size, CSS `clip-path: polygon(25% 25%, 75% 40%, 100% 100%, 0% 100%)`) and a centred `.work-item-name h1`.
  - Enter: `ScrollTrigger.create({trigger: item, start: "top bottom", end: "top top", scrub: 0.5, animation: gsap.fromTo(img, {clipPath: <that polygon>}, {clipPath: "polygon(0% 0%, 100% 0%, 100% 100%, 0% 100%)", ease: "none"})})`.
  - Exit: `{trigger: item, start: "bottom bottom", end: "bottom top", scrub: 0.5}`, `fromTo` ending at `polygon(0% 0%, 100% 0%, 75% 60%, 25% 75%)`.
  - Title: `SplitText.create(h1, {type: "chars", mask: "chars"})`, chars at `y: "125%"`. Each char has its own trigger: `start: "top+=" + (i * 25 - 250) + " top"`, `end: "top+=" + (i * 25 - 100) + " top"`, `scrub: 1`, tween to `y: "0%"`, `ease: "none"`.
  - No pin. Lenis: `lenis.on("scroll", ScrollTrigger.update)`, raf on `gsap.ticker`, `lagSmoothing(0)`.
- **Adapt:** add or remove `.work-item` blocks freely (JS loops over them); polygons and the 25px-per-letter stagger are literals. One ScrollTrigger per letter, so keep titles short. Titles are 5rem (2.5rem under 1000px). No reduced-motion handling.

scroll-29.name: Pinned image mask reveal
scroll-29.text:
- **What you see:** Two columns. Text blocks scroll up on the left; on the right a rounded image frame stays pinned mid-screen. As each new block arrives, the current image is wiped away from its bottom edge upward to reveal the next one beneath, and the page background fades to another pastel.
- **Use for:** pinned storytelling section. A handful of feature blocks (demo: 4), each with heading, paragraph, button and one landscape image (frame up to 540x400).
- **How it works:**
  - `.arch` is a flex row: `.arch__left` with four `.arch__info` blocks (100vh each) and `.arch__right` (100vh) holding four absolutely stacked `.img-wrapper` (400px high, radius 16px). JS copies each wrapper's `data-index` to `z-index`, so the first image is on top.
  - Desktop (`ScrollTrigger.matchMedia`, min-width 769px): one master timeline with `scrollTrigger: {trigger: '.arch', start: 'top top', end: 'bottom bottom', pin: '.arch__right', scrub: true}`.
  - For every image except the last, a sub-timeline is appended: current `img` `clipPath` from `inset(0)` to `inset(0px 0px 100%)` and `objectPosition` from `0px 0%` to `0px 60%` (ease none); next image `objectPosition` to `0px 40%`; `body` `backgroundColor` to `bgColors[i]` (power2.inOut).
  - Mobile (max-width 768px): no pin. CSS `display: contents` plus JS-set flex `order` interleave texts and images; each image gets `{trigger: image, start: 'top-=70% top+=50%', end: 'bottom+=200% bottom', scrub: true}` tweening `objectPosition` 60% to 30%, then the body colour.
  - Lenis (`duration: 1.2`, expo-out easing) runs in a rAF loop: `lenis.raf(time); ScrollTrigger.update()`.
- **Adapt:** add the three libraries yourself (imports plus `gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger)`). The four images are hotlinked from ik.imagekit.io and are not in the zip: s
